## Left open by the earlier read (RD-113)

An independent reader judged the previous rewrite of this lesson. Fix everything below as well. Each item is as serious as an item under "Fix these".

### Findings

1. Rule L12 (Minor). Problem: The English verb in mag-apply is Taglish in teaching prose. A simple Filipino verb such as mag-aplay or humiling can express the idea without switching to English.
   > May mga hindi maaaring mag-apply; kailangan din ang panunumpa at pagpaparehistro.
2. Rule L23 (Major). Problem: The flow instructions overlap: a pre-1973 child of a Filipino mother satisfies the first parent branch, which labels the child natural-born without requiring election. The artist needs an explicit earlier date/parent exception branch before the general parent rule.
   > <!-- ILLUSTRATION: Filipino citizenship flow with labels Magulang na Pilipino sa pagsilang: natural-born; Isinilang bago Enero 17, 1973 sa inang Pilipino at dayuhang ama: wastong pagpili, itinuturing na natural-born; Naturalisasyon: naturalisadong mamamayan -->
extra_brief.lesson-philippine-constitution-the-three:
## Left open by the earlier read (RD-113)

An independent reader judged the previous rewrite of this lesson. Fix everything below as well. Each item is as serious as an item under "Fix these".

### Findings

1. Rule L19 (Major if a step is skipped, otherwise Minor). Problem: The treaty solution requires choosing the two-thirds threshold and then multiplying it by 24. It gives the computation but does not number the two steps. No mathematical step is missing, so this is a minor formatting finding.
   > At least $16$ Senators must concur:
2. Rule L25 (Major). Problem: Public debt, bills of local application, and private bills are listed as origination categories without explaining their meanings. A learner cannot classify those bill types from the teaching provided; no supplied prerequisite teaches them.
   > So must bills increasing public debt, bills of local application, and private bills.
3. Rule L27 (Major). Problem: The lesson acknowledges other pardon limits without stating the election-offense exception requiring COMELEC recommendation. The brief asks for constitutional limits, and an unspecified warning does not teach when the pardon rule applies. This point needs primary-source confirmation because the supplied brief does not quote Article IX-C Section 5.
   > It cannot be used in impeachment cases, and other constitutional limits apply.
